# --- Conventional Commit Template ---
#
# <type>(<scope>): <subject>
#
# <body>
#
# <footer>
#
#
# --- Instructions ---
#
# Type:
#   feat:     A new feature
#   fix:      A bug fix
#   docs:     Documentation only changes
#   style:    Changes that do not affect the meaning of the code (white-space, formatting, etc)
#   refactor: A code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature
#   perf:     A code change that improves performance
#   test:     Adding missing tests or correcting existing tests
#   build:    Changes that affect the build system or external dependencies
#   ci:       Changes to our CI configuration files and scripts
#   chore:    Other changes that don't modify src or test files (e.g., updating dependencies)
#   revert:   Reverts a previous commit
#
# Scope (Optional):
#   A noun describing a section of the codebase (e.g., cli, recruiter, auth, ci, docs).
#
# Subject:
#   A short, imperative-tense description of the change (e.g., "Add 'neofetch' command").
#   - Use the imperative mood (e.g., "add" not "added", "change" not "changed").
#   - Do not capitalize the first letter.
#   - Do not end with a period.
#
# Body (Optional):
#   A more detailed explanation of the changes. Provide context and reasoning.
#   Wrap the body at 72 characters.
#
# Footer (Optional):
#   - For breaking changes: `BREAKING CHANGE: <description>`
#   - For closing issues: `Closes #<issue_number>`, `Fixes #<issue_number>`
#
#
# --- Example ---
#
# feat(cli): add 'show <project>' command with details
#
# Implements the 'show' command which retrieves detailed information
# for a specific project from the backend API.
#
# This includes the project's description, technologies, and all
# available links (live, github, pypi, etc.).
#
# Fixes #12
